Can a “Homemaker” Be Only a Woman? ⚖️
A recent observation of the Madras High Court has started an important conversation about marriage, careers and the economic value of unpaid household work.
In V v. A, CMA(MD) No.1257 of 2024, the Madras High Court observed that as traditional family roles change and more women pursue demanding careers, husbands too can choose to become homemakers.
The Court emphasised that the expression “homemaker” is gender-neutral and that domestic work carries real economic value.
But the larger legal lesson, in my view, is more important than the headline.
A marriage is not simply:
One earns → One manages the home.
Both financial contribution and unpaid domestic contribution can have significance within a family.
The case also reminds us that matrimonial disputes are rarely about a single disagreement. Career choices, residence, children, financial dependence, expectations and responsibilities can all become part of the legal and human context.
Law does not operate in isolation from changing social realities.
For lawyers, the challenge is to understand both:
the legal rights
and
the facts that created the dispute.
That is where meaningful matrimonial litigation begins.
Case: V v. A
Madras High Court, Madurai Bench
CMA(MD) No.1257 of 2024
2026 LiveLaw (Mad) 460
What should a modern marriage recognise first—
equality of roles, equality of economic contribution, or equality of responsibilities?
Adv. Smriti Kumari (Tiwari)
Advocate, Patna High Court
